findings: The detector is interior stationary population divided by the left incident flux, with no right incidence and no postselection. This is a distinct physical observable from the supplied incident-column scattering time delay.

The two-face phase conventions make free transmission exp(i*k*L), so both controls give L/k in calibration and identify width. The finite-energy transfer derivative includes both interior propagation and energy-dependent lead momentum.
The physical density identity is tau_dwell=Im(S_column_dagger*dS_column/dE)+Im(r)/(2E). The additional boundary term has the correct sign for the left incident/reflected interference.

The independent reference solves all four interface amplitude conditions and integrates the coherent interior wave density, divided by incident speed k. Its cosine and sine-over-q basis remains regular at the barrier top.

An independent weak negative-imaginary potential loses probability at twice its magnitude times the interior population. The extrapolated absorption loss confirms the occupancy definition and boundary-term sign.

Public wording defines the detector and phase conventions without naming the missing interference correction or requiring a scattering-derivative method. Numerical density integration and other valid representations remain allowed.
